historyTimeline.h2: Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 2.0 TDCi variant launched, it served as the high-torque, long-distance workhorse of the Ford Focus range. Over its production run, Ford refined the Duratorq TDCi architecture to improve emissions and reliability, though core mechanical layouts remained consistent.

milestones.description: G6DA / G6DB introduced, 2.0L Duratorq TDCi, 100kW (136hp) / 81kW (110hp), replacing older non-common-rail diesels in the Mk2 Focus.
G6DG variant introduced for the Mk2 facelift, offering 96kW (130hp) with updated engine management and improved DPF integration.

Mk3 Focus launched; while 1.6 TDCi became the dominant diesel, select higher-spec 2.0 TDCi variants continued with updated emissions hardware before being phased out in favour of 1.5/2.0 EcoBlue in later generations.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi is generally a robust Duratorq unit, but high-mileage examples are prone to specific emissions and fuel system failures. The G6DA, G6DB, and G6DG codes dominate replacement demand for this variant. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF & EGR Clogging - Why the Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi (G6DA/G6DB/G6DG) Suffers Premature Blockages
problems.rootCause: Frequent short, low-speed urban journeys prevent the Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) from reaching the high temperatures required for active regeneration. Soot accumulates, increasing backpressure and forcing the EGR valve to stick open, which can eventually lead to turbo starvation or engine limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical clean of DPF and EGR valve, ECU reset
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix; blockage will return if driving habits do not change

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Fit new or pattern DPF, replace associated sensors
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if the engine block and turbo are confirmed healthy

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if DPF failure has caused secondary turbo or piston ring damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi of relevant age (2004-2011) is currently valued between £1,200 and £5,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.
problems.recommendation: If the engine is otherwise running well with no bottom-end noise, a specialist DPF clean and EGR service is the most cost-effective first step. However, if the blockage has triggered a turbo failure or severe oil contamination, a reconditioned engine is often more economical than repairing the ancillaries on a high-mileage block.

problems.h4: Injector Seal Failure ("Black Death") - Why the Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi (G6DA/G6DB) Develops Carbon Buildup
problems.rootCause: The copper sealing washer at the base of the fuel injector degrades over time due to heat cycles. This allows combustion gases to escape, creating a hard, tar-like carbon deposit around the injector base that can eventually seize the injector in the cylinder head.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injectors, clean carbon, fit new copper seals and retainers
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended as preventative maintenance at 80k miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply and fit a single new or refurbished injector
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if only one injector is leaking and the head is undamaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary only if seized injectors have caused cylinder head cracking or severe internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi of relevant age (2004-2011) is currently valued between £1,200 and £5,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.
problems.recommendation: Injector seal replacement is a relatively inexpensive and highly effective preventative measure. Do not ignore the smell of exhaust fumes in the cabin. If caught early, seal replacement saves the engine. Full replacement is only justified if the cylinder head has been compromised by a severely seized injector.

items.question: What are the signs of DPF failure in a Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi?
items.answer: DPF failure in the Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi usually presents as a persistent engine management light, reduced power (limp mode), and poor fuel economy.
keyPoints: You may notice a strong smell of sulfur or diesel from the exhaust.
The vehicle may refuse to regenerate, leading to increased exhaust backpressure.
Ignoring these signs can lead to secondary turbocharger damage.

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi?
items.answer: For a Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi valued between £1,200 and £5,000, a full rebuilt engine may approach or exceed 60% of the vehicle's value.
keyPoints: If the vehicle is in excellent cosmetic and mechanical condition otherwise, a reconditioned engine with a 12-month warranty is a sound investment.
For lower-value examples, a quality used engine or targeted repair (like a DPF clean) is often the most financially sensible route.
Always evaluate scrap or part-exchange value before committing to a full rebuild.

items.question: What is the difference between the G6DA and G6DB Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi engines?
items.answer: The primary difference between the G6DA and G6DB codes fitted to the Ford Focus 2.0 TDCi is the power output and associated engine mapping.
keyPoints: The G6DA produces 100kW (136hp) and was often fitted to higher-spec Zetec and Ghia trims.
The G6DB produces 81kW (110hp) and was commonly found in LX and base Zetec models.
Mechanically, they share the same core Duratorq block, but ECU tuning and some turbo components differ.
